# Copilot Instructions

When generating or modifying code, follow these principles:

- Write clean, readable, maintainable code.
- Prefer small, focused functions and classes with a single responsibility.
- Follow SOLID principles:
  - Single Responsibility Principle
  - Open/Closed Principle
  - Liskov Substitution Principle
  - Interface Segregation Principle
  - Dependency Inversion Principle
- Keep code DRY and avoid unnecessary duplication.
- Favor explicit, descriptive names over short abbreviations.
- Handle errors gracefully and add meaningful validation.
- Prefer configuration over hardcoded values when appropriate.
- Keep changes minimal, targeted, and easy to review.
- When writing prompts or generating code, prefer concise instructions that use the fewest tokens necessary while still producing high-quality results.
- Be explicit about the goal, constraints, and required output format to avoid unnecessary back-and-forth.
- When suggesting code, explain the reasoning briefly and include practical examples when useful.
